about: Anchors are the places where things attach. Each anchor has a stable id rule (no rules version in it), so the stable dice give the same objects after an update (gotcha 8.12), and one owner tile (hash of the stable id), so objects on a tile border are made once (gotcha 8.3).

anchors.found_by: OSM way centreline + CORR cross-section (edge of travelled way, shoulder, kerb, verge, ditch)
anchors.fallback: class width table when the cross-section is missing
anchors.stable_id: hash(osm way id, side, 10 m station index from the way start)
anchors.stable_id_note: if the way is split or merged in a newer OSM, stations move; use the way's first node id + the along distance from that node as a second key; T8 measures churn
anchors.offset_reference: the outer edge of the travelled way (paint line or pavement edge); kerb face where a kerb exists

anchors.found_by: OSM service=driveway ways; else derived: one per house footprint (Microsoft or Overture) that faces a road within 60 m, at the lot frontage, on the garage side when the footprint shows an attached garage
anchors.fallback: derived position with p_exist 0.9 for houses on dens:1-3 roads
anchors.stable_id: hash(osm way id) or hash(footprint id, road way id)

anchors.found_by: OSM node shared by two or more drivable ways (driveways and parking aisles do not count)
each way that enters a junction; the sign point is 3-15 m before the junction on the right side
anchors.stable_id: hash(junction node id, entering way id)

anchors.found_by: geometry: a run of the way where the fitted radius is below 600 m (2000 ft), with its start (PC), end (PT), radius, and direction; the CORR cross-section gives superelevation
anchors.stable_id: hash(osm way id, index of the curve along the way)

anchors.found_by: OSM maxspeed tag differs between two joined ways, or a node with maxspeed change
OSM waterway or NHD flowline crosses a road way; type culvert, bridge or ford from the tags (tunnel=culvert, bridge=*) and NBI for bridges
anchors.stable_id: hash(waterway way id, road way id)

anchors.found_by: anchor:driveway where the CORR cross-section has a ditch on that side
the footprint edge that faces the nearest road (Microsoft, Overture or OSM footprint)
later: county parcel lines where the licence allows; now: the line half way between two neighbouring footprints, from the road back to the rear of the footprints
